newsitem.title: INDIA: India ITC conducts internal forex audit.
newsitem.headline: India ITC conducts internal forex audit.

text.p: Indian tobacco giant ITC Ltd is carrying out an audit to probe a suspected violation of foreign exchange rules in the firm, an investigator said on Tuesday.

A spokeswoman for ITC, in which Britain's B.A.T. Industries plc holds more than 31 percent, said the company had agreed to probe suspected violation of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) in one of its departments.

Investigators quizzed Yogesh Deveshwar, ITC's chairman, for more than 18 hours on Monday and Tuesday in the investigations for which two former chairmen were arrested by the Enforcement Directorate last week.

"Mr Deveshwar has admitted that there is suspected FERA violation to the tune of around $2.0 million through under invoicing on tobacco export by the India Leaf Tobacco Division between 1991 and April 1996," K K Kabirpanthi of the Enforcement Directorate told reporters in Calcutta.
"Yes, the internal audit investigation into FERA violation is on," an ITC spokeswoman told Reuters.
"Mr Deveshwar said his internal audit (department) had been investigating suspected FERA violation and he would submit a report to us within 15 days," Kabirpanthi said.
"I am fully cooperating with the investigating agency. The interrogation will contitue. They are all professional people," Deveshwar told reporters after his interrogation.
Kabirpanthi said the enforcement officials would also examine B.A.T. nominees who are on ITC's board.
"We are going to examine the BAT nominees and we have given 15 days' time to the ITC chairman to call them. Anyway they are coming," Kabirpanthi added.
B.A.T. said on Monday that it was willing to cooperate with the investigation by Indian authorities.
